chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sallam, from Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn Isam, from Dawood al-Raqqi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I had some wealth upon a man, and I feared it would be lost. So I complained to him about that. He said to me: 'When you go to Makkah, perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abdul Muttalib and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abu Talib and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abdullah and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Amina and pray two Rak'ahs on her behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Fatima bint Asad and pray two Rak'ahs on her behalf. Then supplicate that your wealth be returned to you.'
He said: 'So I did that. Then I went out from the Door of Al-Safa, and there was my debtor standing there saying, 'O Dawood! You withheld me for long. Come, take possession of your wealth'.'

key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ أَسَدٍ: Fatima bint Asad (mother of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What ritual acts did Imam al-Sadiq recommend for recovering lost wealth or debts?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia practice of *Tawaf al-Nawafil* (voluntary circumambulation) performed on behalf of the deceased, specifically highlighting the intercessory merit of the Prophet’s immediate family. The narrative underscores the spiritual efficacy of combining ritual devotion with supplication (*dua*) to resolve worldly concerns, as evidenced by the immediate recovery of Dawood al-Raqqi’s debt. It reflects the broader theological belief in the continued influence of the Ahl al-Bayt in the spiritual and material realms.
